tree: Margin vs markup: how the calculator works
Both use the same profit, but divide it by different numbers. Margin compares profit to the selling price. Markup compares profit to the cost.

tree: What is the difference between margin and markup?
Margin is profit as a share of the selling price. Markup is profit as a share of the cost. The same $40 profit on a $60 cost and $100 price is a 40% margin but a 66.67% markup.

tree.style: display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; min-height:60px; padding:14px 0; font-size:17px; font-weight:700

tree: How do I set a price for a target margin?
Divide the cost by one minus the margin. For a 30% margin on a $14 cost: $14 ÷ 0.70 = $20. Choose “Price from margin” to calculate it.

tree.style: display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; min-height:60px; padding:14px 0; font-size:17px; font-weight:700

tree: Why can’t margin be 100% or more?
Margin is profit divided by price, and profit can never be larger than the price. A 100% margin only happens when the cost is zero. Markup has no such limit.

tree.style: display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; min-height:60px; padding:14px 0; font-size:17px; font-weight:700

tree: Is this gross margin or net margin?
Gross margin. It uses the cost of each unit only. Net margin also subtracts overheads such as rent, wages and marketing, which this calculator doesn’t ask for.

tree.style: display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; min-height:60px; padding:14px 0; font-size:17px; font-weight:700

tree: Should I include sales tax in the price?
No. Use the price before sales tax, because the tax isn’t income for your business.

tree.style: display:flex; align-items:center; gap:14px; min-height:60px; padding:14px 0; font-size:17px; font-weight:700

tree: Does Noxtill store the numbers I enter?
No. The calculation runs in your browser. The values aren’t sent to Noxtill, added to the page address or saved in browser storage.
